en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Vessantara, Concerning the Question on Inference.
10. The Question on the Form and Shape of Nibbāna “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say, ‘Nibbāna, Nibbāna,’ is it possible to point out,
by way of simile, reason, cause, or method, either the form or the shape, or the duration or the measure of that Nibbāna?”
“Nirvana, Great King, is without counterpart; it is not possible to demonstrate the form, the shape, the duration, or the measure of Nirvana by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method.

“Venerable Nāgasena, I do not accept this either—that for Nirvana, which is an existing reality, there can be no demonstration of its form, its shape, its duration, or its measure by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method.”
“Convince me by means of a reason.
“Very well, great king, I shall convince you by means of a reason.
Great king, is there such a thing as the so-called great ocean?”
“Yes, venerable sir, there is this great ocean.
“If someone were to ask you, Great King, ‘Great King, how much water is there in the great ocean,
and how many beings dwell within the great ocean?’— being asked thus, Great King, what would you say?”
“...you should explain it to him.

“Venerable sir, if someone were to ask me, ‘Great King, how much water is there in the great ocean, and how many beings dwell within the great ocean?’—venerable sir, I would say to him: ‘That is not a question that should be asked.’”
“‘O good man, you ask me this; this question is not one that should be asked by anyone.

This is a question to be set aside. The great ocean has not been analyzed by the world-expounders; it is impossible to measure the water in the great ocean, or the beings who have taken up residence there. Thus, Bhante, would I give him my reply.
“But why, Great King, would you give such a reply regarding the great ocean, which is an existing reality? Is it not so?”
“Having calculated it, one should declare to him: ‘So much water is in the great ocean, and so many beings dwell within the great ocean.
“It is not possible, Bhante; this question is beyond the scope [of calculation].
“Just as, Great King, even though the great ocean is a reality that exists, it is impossible to calculate the amount of its water, or the number of beings who have taken up residence there.”

In the same way, Great King, it is impossible to demonstrate by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method the form, shape, age, or measure of Nibbāna, which is indeed an existing reality. Even if, Great King,
a possessor of psychic power who has attained mastery over the mind were to count the water in the great ocean and the beings dwelling therein, he could not do so [in the case of Nibbāna].

Even one possessed of psychic power who has attained mastery over the mind might be able to demonstrate, by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method, the form, shape, duration, or measure of Nibbāna.
Furthermore, O Great King, hear another further reason: it is simply because Nibbāna is a non-existent phenomenon that it cannot be demonstrated.
“It is impossible to demonstrate form, or shape, or age, or size, by way of simile, or reason, or cause, or method.
“There are, Great King, among the devas those known as the Arūpakāyika devas.
“Yes, venerable sir, it is heard that there are among the devas those known as the Arūpakāyika devas.”

“But, great king, is it possible to point out, by way of a simile, a reason, a cause, a method, or an illustration, the form, the shape, the age, or the size of those gods who belong to the formless body?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.
“In that case, great king, there are no gods who belong to the formless body?”

“There are, venerable sir, gods belonging to the formless body, and it is not possible to demonstrate their form, or shape, or age, or measure, either by way of simile, or reason, or cause, or method.

“Just as, great king, although there truly exist those gods belonging to the formless body, it is not possible to demonstrate their form, or shape, or age, or measure, either by way of simile, or reason, or cause, or method;”
“In the same way, Great King, although Nibbāna is an existing reality, it is impossible to point out its form, shape, age, or measure by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method.
“Venerable Nāgasena, let it be that Nibbāna is exclusively blissful, and that its form, shape, age, or measure cannot be pointed out by means of a simile, a reason, a cause, or a method.”
“But, venerable sir, is there any quality of Nibbāna that has been entered into by others, even as a mere illustration through a simile?
“In its own form, great king, there is none; but in terms of its qualities, it is possible to point to some mere illustration through a simile.

“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! Speak quickly so that I may obtain even a partial indication of the qualities of Nibbāna; extinguish the fever of my heart and dispel it with the breeze of your cool and sweet speech.”
“Great King, one quality of the lotus has entered into Nibbāna; two qualities of water, three qualities of an antidote,
four qualities of the great ocean, five qualities of food, ten qualities of space,
three qualities of the jewel-treasure, three qualities of red sandalwood, and three qualities of the cream of ghee have entered into the mountain peak.”
“Five qualities have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that one quality of the lotus has entered into Nibbāna—which one quality of the lotus has entered into Nibbāna?
“Just as, Great King, the lotus is unsullied by water;”
“Even so, Great King, Nibbāna is unsullied by all defilements.
This, Great King, is one quality of the lotus that has entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that two qualities of water have entered into Nibbāna—which are those two qualities of water that have entered into Nibbāna?”
“Just as water, O Great King, is cool and quenches the fever of burning,
even so, O Great King, is Nibbāna cool and quenches the fever of all defilements.
This, O Great King, is the first quality of water inherent in Nibbāna.”
Furthermore, great king, water is the quenching of thirst for the multitudes of people and animals who are exhausted, weary, thirsty, and scorched by the heat;
even so, great king, Nibbāna is the quenching of the thirst of craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence.
This, great king, is the second quality of water inherent in Nibbāna.
“Great King, these two qualities of water have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that ‘three qualities of an antidote have entered into Nibbāna’—what are those three qualities of an antidote that have entered into Nibbāna?
“Just as, Great King, an antidote is a refuge for beings afflicted by poison;”
In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is the refuge for beings oppressed by the poison of the defilements.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the antidote inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, the antidote brings an end to diseases.
In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna brings an end to all suffering.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the antidote inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, the antidote is the Deathless.
"In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is the deathless.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the medicine that has entered into Nibbāna.
These, Great King, are the three qualities of the medicine that have entered into Nibbāna."
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say— that ‘four qualities of the great ocean have entered into Nibbāna’— which four qualities of the great ocean have entered into Nibbāna?
“Just as, Great King, the great ocean is empty of all refuse, even so, Great King, Nibbāna is empty of the refuse of all defilements.”
This, great king, is the first quality of the great ocean that has entered into Nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, great king, the great ocean is vast and boundless, and it is not filled even by all the rivers flowing into it;
even so, great king, Nirvāṇa is vast and boundless, and it is not filled by all sentient beings.
This, great king, is the second quality of the great ocean that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, the great ocean is the abode of mighty beings;
even so, great king, Nibbāna is the abode of the mighty Arahants—those great beings who have attained power through the strength of their taintless and stainless states.
This, great king, is the third quality of the great ocean that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, the great ocean is in full bloom with immeasurable, diverse, and vast waves as its flowers;
even so, great king, Nibbāna is in full bloom with immeasurable, diverse, and vast flowers of purified true knowledge and liberation.
“This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the great ocean that has entered into Nibbāna.
These, Great King, are the four qualities of the great ocean that have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘five qualities of food have entered into Nibbāna’—what are those five qualities of food that have entered into Nibbāna?”
“Just as food, Great King, maintains the life-force of all beings,
even so, Great King, Nibbāna, when realized, maintains the life-force by destroying aging and death.
This, Great King, is the first quality of food inherent in Nibbāna.”
Furthermore, Great King, food increases the strength of all beings;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna, when realized, increases the power of psychic success for all beings.
This, Great King, is the second quality of food inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, food produces physical beauty in all beings;
in the same way, great king, Nibbāna, when realized, produces the beauty of virtue in all beings.
This, great king, is the third quality of food inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, food allays the exhaustion of all beings;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna, when realized, allays the exhaustion of all defilements for all beings.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of food that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, food dispels the weakness of hunger for all beings;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna, when realized, dispels the weakness of the hunger of all suffering for all beings.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of food that has entered into Nibbāna.
“Great King, these five qualities of food have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that ten qualities of space have entered into Nibbāna—which are those ten qualities of space that have entered into Nibbāna?

“Great King, just as space is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear; it is difficult to overcome, it cannot be stolen by thieves, it is independent, it is the path of birds, it is unobstructed, and it is infinite.”

“In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear; it is difficult to overcome, it cannot be stolen by thieves, it is independent, it is the path traveled by the Noble Ones, it is unobstructed, and it is infinite.
These, Great King, are the ten qualities of space that have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that ‘three qualities of the jewel-treasure have entered into Nibbāna’—which are those three qualities of the jewel-treasure that have entered into Nibbāna?”
“Just as, Great King, the jewel-treasure grants all desires;
even so, Great King, does Nibbāna grant all desires.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the jewel-treasure inherent in Nibbāna.”
Furthermore, great king, the jewel-treasure brings laughter;
even so, great king, Nibbāna brings laughter.
This, great king, is the second quality of the jewel-treasure inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, the jewel-treasure produces radiance;
even so, great king, does Nibbāna produce radiance.
This, great king, is the third quality of the jewel-treasure inherent in Nibbāna.
“These three qualities of the jewel-treasure, O Great King, have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘three qualities of red sandalwood have entered into Nibbāna’—what are those three qualities of red sandalwood that have entered into Nibbāna?
“Just as, O Great King, red sandalwood is difficult to find;”
In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is difficult to attain.
This, Great King, is the first quality of red sandalwood that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, red sandalwood possesses an incomparable fragrance.
In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is unequaled in its sweet fragrance.
This, Great King, is the second quality of red sandalwood that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, red sandalwood is praised by the virtuous.
"In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna is praised by noble and virtuous persons.
This, Great King, is the third quality of red sandalwood that has entered into Nibbāna.
These, Great King, are the three qualities of red sandalwood that have entered into Nibbāna."
“Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three qualities of the cream of ghee have entered into Nibbāna,’ what are those three qualities of the cream of ghee that have entered into Nibbāna?
“Just as, Great King, the cream of ghee is endowed with beauty of color,
even so, Great King, Nibbāna is endowed with the beauty of its qualities.”
This, great king, is the first quality of the cream of ghee that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, the cream of ghee is endowed with fragrance;
even so, great king, is Nibbāna endowed with the fragrance of virtue.
This, great king, is the second quality of the cream of ghee that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, great king, the cream of ghee is endowed with flavor;
even so, great king, Nibbāna is endowed with flavor.
“This, O Great King, is the third quality of the cream of ghee that has entered into Nibbāna.
These, O Great King, are the three qualities of the cream of ghee that have entered into Nibbāna.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that five qualities of a mountain peak have entered into Nibbāna—which are those five qualities of a mountain peak that have entered into Nibbāna?”
“Just as, Great King, a mountain peak is loftily risen;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna is loftily risen.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the mountain peak that has entered into Nibbāna.”
Furthermore, great king, a mountain peak is immovable;
even so, great king, Nibbāna is immovable.
This, great king, is the second quality of the mountain peak that has entered into Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, a mountain peak is difficult to ascend;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna is difficult to ascend for all defilements.
This, Great King, is the third quality of a mountain peak inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, just as a mountain peak is a place where no seeds can sprout,
even so, Great King, Nibbāna is a state where all defilements cannot sprout.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the mountain peak inherent in Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, the mountain peak is free from attraction and aversion;
even so, Great King, Nibbāna is free from attraction and aversion.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the mountain peak that has entered into Nibbāna.
“These, O Great King, are the five qualities of the mountain peak that have entered into Nibbāna.
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.
The tenth dilemma: The Form and Shape of Nibbāna.
